status: Native non-LFR boss generation now honors saved recipient cooldowns; shared loot retains an eligibility snapshot. Automated checks pass; client/real encounter checks remain pending.
defect: Actual Unit::GeneratePersonalLoot already excluded saved players from the equipment lottery, but its non-LFR per-player generation still ran for them. Shared quest caches also admitted them. Native Guarm114323 and Helya114537 generated more fragments on a repeated Normal/Heroic/Mythic source; a saved member could receive a fresh group's fragments under PERSONAL_LOOT, GROUP_LOOT and MASTER_LOOT. LFR repeated generation already rejected saved recipients.
fix: Copy the native pre-roll eligible GUID list before equipment recipient selection. Skip saved personal recipients while preserving the independent bonus-roll prompt. If none are eligible, preserve existing containers and return before fresh shared generation.

Pass the snapshot to an additional FillLoot overload; preserve the existing overload/API for ordinary callers. Stamp shared items/quest items with restricted allowedGUIDs before caches are built, filter recipients during cache construction, and enforce the restriction in actual LootItem::AllowedForPlayer. This protects cached view/slot/roll/master admission without denying already-earned loot after its cooldown is marked.

Record remaining fresh shared recipients' cooldowns as well. LootItem's added bit uses padding before its existing pointer; the MSVC x64 native probe asserts size0x78 and m_loot offset0x68 for the pinned library comparison. The full production game/scripts build is rebuilt with the new header; no old/new runtime library mixing.

native_probe.result: Both processes exit0, DBErrors0 bytes. Pinned-library PASS asserts the old repeated grants; current asserts denial. The final probe additionally covers the two separate chest/LFR fixes linked below.
coverage: Full actual Unit::GeneratePersonalLoot, Loot::FillLoot, row selection, cache admission, packet serialization and actual StoreLootItem/AutoStoreItems inventory receipt for both bosses and LFR17/Normal14/Heroic15/Mythic16. Five real native Player/session objects share an actual Group/raid membership and InstanceMap; LFR's native lottery produces at least four equipment non-winners who still receive fragments.

Fresh sources for the same saved players cannot grant again. Mixed saved/fresh membership is tested under PERSONAL_LOOT/GROUP_LOOT/MASTER_LOOT; the four fresh participants retain their fragments. Actual admission rejects absent quest, COMPLETE quest and1000-fragment quota while independent unfinished recipients still receive theirs.

Actual Unit::Kill for both bosses/all four difficulties with a full inventory tests earned shared-container retry after cooldown and duplicate receipt. Initial tap/damage-requirement input is seeded; this is not a boss combat-AI or lethal spell-damage test.

Actual SaveToDB writes inventory/cooldowns, and a new same-GUID Player loads native prepared inventory/cooldown results. Sequential LFR/Normal/Heroic/Mythic awards remain independent; repeated Normal is denied after reload. Separate characters keep each boss source below the1000 quota. No scheduled weekly reset or authenticated login is simulated.
native_probe.data: Native7.3.5 DB2/hotfix bootstrap and full configured rows for creature loot114323/114537 and chest loot70585. Existing personal-loot mappings, gameobject templates, instance encounters, page texts, area-trigger teleports, LFG data and random enchantment loaders execute. Scoped raid rows have no references or source1/source4 conditions; the probe refuses changed condition catalogs. Luck/zone/currency catalogs outside these selected rows are not a complete world-loot catalog test.
native_probe.isolation: Read-only World/Hotfix pools; schema-only disposable character/auth databases (167 tables), restricted disposable user, no personal rows copied/written. Initial membership/accepted quest and future weekly reset time are fixtures. Native loaders, selectors, receipt and SQL persistence are real. The two schemas and user are removed in finally.
native_probe.development_failures: Initial harness omitted LFG bootstrap and crashed in its lookup, then omitted teleport/page-text/random-enchantment dependencies and emitted loader errors. These setup failures were corrected with native loader ordering; no error log was suppressed and no partial run was accepted as passing.

regressions: Test-LostArmy.ps1 and Test-BossQuestLoot.ps1 pass. The extracted condition fixture now explicitly defaults unrestricted admission and supplies allowedGUIDs/const GUID lookup; it does not replace the full native snapshot test.

Full native LostArmy run-20261019-101526, MasterLoot run-20261019-101547, RollCompletion run-20261019-101607, GroupRollLifecycle run-20261019-101554 and LostArmyTurnIn run-20261019-101528 pass with empty DBErrors logs.

Test-RaidFragmentsRelease.ps1 verifies the canonical snapshot overload call, item restriction bit branch and final-link source/header freshness, alongside the existing loot/roll/group/quest-turn-in binary checks.

deployment.build: cmake --build build-extractors --config Release --target worldserver bnetserver --parallel 4; no OutDir override; full header rebuild followed by final Unit rebuild

limitations: Controlled defeated actors use live templates with NullCreatureAI and a base InstanceScript on map1648; the retail encounter script, matchmaking/entry, participation/range policy, legal character creation, other classes/factions and client looting are not exercised. Most cases enter the full loot generator directly; the full-bag cases also execute real Unit::Kill.

Sessions are socketless process-lifetime allocations. Native prepared loading is not Player::LoadFromDB/authenticated relog or the World scheduler. Weekly reset time is seeded in the future; actual wall-clock rollover/reset scheduling is unverified.

Drop counts/chances/modes are unchanged. Existing Helya100..150 and Rockaway10..15 remain explicit reconstructions, not newly established retail distributions. No complete raid/client verification is claimed.
